newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil petroleum bill faces vote in Congress.
newsitem.headline: Brazil petroleum bill faces vote in Congress.

text.p: A bill regulating the opening up of Brazil's petroleum industry to the private sector is expected to be put to a vote in a Chamber of Deputies panel later on Wednesday, congressional officials said.

The committee was due to meet at 1000 local/1300 GMT with the intention of voting on the bill. If approved, the bill will probably be sent for a vote on the floor of the Chamber of Deputies. It also has to pass through the Senate.
Deputy Eliseu Resende, in charge of drawing up the law, spent Tuesday night sifting through about 100 proposed amendments, "but there won't be any big changes," an aide said.

The bill would allow private companies to compete or go into partnership with state oil and gas giant Petrobras. It would also create a new regulator to oversee the oil and gas sector and end fuel price subsidies within three years.
Newspapers said unresolved differences among members of the 30-strong committee might cause the vote to be delayed.
The legislation has been criticized by proponents of privatization for ruling out the possibility of the state giving up its controlling stake in Petrobras.
Left-wing opposition parties also object to the bill, saying it will allow Petrobras' assets, such as its refineries, to be sold to the private sector.
